content: This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine tests, potentially leading to inaccurate results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). If the situation is less critical, contact a poison control center without delay. For residents in the United States, the poison control hotline is 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current medical condition. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your healthcare provider. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to compensate for the missed one. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal regulations. This information was last updated in August 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for comprehensive information about this medication and your individual health needs. Common side effects of this medication may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain or cramping, and loss of appetite. Taking the medication with food may help alleviate these symptoms. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. In rare cases, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacterial infection with Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or even weeks to months after treatment has ended. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Before taking erythromycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other macrolide antibiotics (such as azithromycin or clarithromycin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Erythromycin may cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm, known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also increase the risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be heightened if you are using certain drugs (such as diuretics or water pills) or if you have conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Erythromycin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Some erythromycin products may contain sodium, which should be considered if you are on a sodium-restricted diet. This medication passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of erythromycin from your body, which could impact how it works. Similarly, erythromycin can slow the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially affecting their efficacy. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine tests, potentially causing false test results. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your healthcare provider. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in August 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
